title: Solo leaderboards miss correlated model blind spots and multi-agent error compounding
text: Unlike human specialists whose strengths and gaps differ across individuals, copies of an AI model share correlated jaggedness—adding capacity without complementary breadth. Because single-agent benchmarks test models in isolation, they overstate competitive readiness against mosaic human teams; evaluation must expand to organizational benchmarks measuring task decomposition, clean state handoffs, and whether agents catch rather than compound each other’s errors.
qualification: Normative critique of prevailing AI leaderboards synthesizing arXiv:2512.15567 on correlated AI errors and arXiv:2611.05417; standard multi-agent organizational benchmarks remain nascent.

public_locator.value: Alongside individual leaderboards, we need benchmarks for organizations of agents: measuring how well multi-agent systems divide unfamiliar problems without duplicating work, share context cleanly across handoffs, and catch rather than compound one another’s mistakes over long horizons.
